First release: Socialite login, keycloak.web / keycloak.api middleware, users / roles / groups services.

docs.title: Web SSO
docs.text: The browser login uses the OpenID Connect authorization code flow with PKCE, through a Socialite driver. After login the Keycloak tokens are stored in the Laravel session, and the user is logged into your normal Laravel guard, so auth()->user(), @auth and policies work as usual.

docs.title: Protect routes
docs.text:
Route::middleware(['web', 'keycloak.web'])->group(function () {
    Route::get('/dashboard', DashboardController::class);
});

// a specific guard (realm + client)
Route::middleware(['web', 'keycloak.web:partner-portal'])->group(/* ... */);

What keycloak.web does on every request:

  1. Guest? It remembers the URL and redirects to the Keycloak login page. JSON requests get a 401 instead.
  2. Access token about to expire? It refreshes the token silently with the refresh token. If Keycloak refuses (the session ended, the user was disabled), the user is logged out and sent back to log in.
  3. Otherwise it lets the request through without any call to Keycloak.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
The package registers three routes (prefix and names are configurable):

Route Name Purpose GET /auth/keycloak/login/{guard?} keycloak.login Start the login. ?redirect=/reports sets where to land afterwards (local URLs only). GET /auth/keycloak/callback/{guard?} keycloak.callback OAuth callback. Register this URL in Keycloak. GET /auth/keycloak/logout/{guard?} keycloak.logout Log out locally and at Keycloak, then come back. 
<a href="{{ route('keycloak.login', ['guard' => 'web']) }}">Sign in</a>
<a href="{{ route('keycloak.logout') }}">Sign out</a>

On the callback the package:

  • exchanges the code (with the PKCE verifier) and reads the userinfo,
  • creates or updates the local user from the claims (provisioning),
  • logs them in and regenerates the session to prevent session fixation,
  • stores the access, refresh and ID tokens in the session,
  • dispatches UserLoggedIn, then redirects to the remembered URL, the intended URL, or web.home.

A stale or replayed callback (back button, expired session, already-used code) just starts the login again.

docs.title: Logout
docs.text:
keycloak.logout uses RP-initiated logout: it sends id_token_hint, client_id and post_logout_redirect_uri, so Keycloak ends the SSO session without a confirmation page and sends the browser back to redirect_after_logout. Add that URL to Valid post logout redirect URIs on the client.

To end a session from the server side (for example an API logout endpoint), use the back-channel logout: Keycloak::oidc()->logout($refreshToken).

docs.title: Session validation
docs.text:
web.validation Cost per request Detects a session ended in Keycloak local (default) none: compares the expiry time at the next refresh (within the access-token lifespan, 5 minutes by default) introspect one cached call per token.introspection_cache_ttl within the cache TTL (default 30s)

local is the right choice for most apps. The 1.x version called introspection on every request, which added a round-trip to Keycloak to every page view. Use introspect when you need near-instant revocation, and shorten the access-token lifespan in Keycloak if you need both.

docs.title: Reading the user and the token
docs.text:
$user  = auth()->user();            // your users model (KCUserModel by default)
$token = Keycloak::token();         // KeycloakToken from the session

$token->roles();                    // ['admin', 'editor']
$token->hasRole('admin');
$user->hasRole('admin');            // with the HasKeycloakRoles trait
session('keycloak_token');          // raw access token

See Authorization for every role, scope and group helper.

docs.title: Admin panels (Filament, Nova, ...)
docs.text:
Add the middleware to the panel's auth middleware stack:

// app/Providers/Filament/AdminPanelProvider.php
->authMiddleware([
    \Bhry98\KeycloakAuth\Http\Middleware\KeycloakMiddleware::class,
])

and make the panel's login action point to route('keycloak.login'). To restrict the panel to a role, add canAccessPanel() to your user model:

public function canAccessPanel(Panel $panel): bool
{
    return $this->hasRole('admin'); // HasKeycloakRoles
}

docs.title: Several realms or clients
docs.text:
Each guard has its own login and callback route:

'guard' => [
    'web' => [...],
    'partners' => ['realm' => 'partners', 'client_id' => 'portal', 'redirect' => env('APP_URL').'/auth/keycloak/callback/partners'],
],

Route::middleware(['web', 'keycloak.web:partners'])->prefix('partners')->group(/* ... */);

Use the guard's auth_guard option to log each realm into a separate Laravel guard, for example 'auth_guard' => 'partners' with a session guard of that name in config/auth.php.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Event When UserLoggedIn after a successful callback ($user, $token, $guard) TokenRefreshed after a silent refresh ($token, $guard) UserLoggedOut in the logout route ($user, $guard) UserProvisioned when the local user row was created or changed ($user, $token, $created)

docs.title: Laravel API Response
docs.text:
GitHub Packagist Get started

A fluent, extensible, highly configurable API response toolkit for Laravel 11, 12, 13 and 14. It works with zero configuration, and you can customize it as far as you need.

return api()->created($user);

return api()
    ->success()
    ->message('User created.')
    ->data($user)
    ->meta(['foo' => 'bar'])
    ->headers(['X-Foo' => 'bar'])
    ->send();

docs.title: Why this package
docs.text:
• One fluent builder (api() / ApiResponse) for every response your API sends: success, error, validation, pagination, resources.
  • Configurable envelope: rename keys, wrap the payload, switch between default/minimal/mobile/jsonapi presets, or write your own formatter.
  • Automatic data detection: pass an Eloquent model, a Collection, a JsonResource, a paginator, or a plain array/DTO, and it's normalized the same way every time.
  • Opt-in middleware for cross-cutting concerns: rate limiting, request/response audit logging, and Accept-Language-aware locale resolution, all driven by config.
  • Hooks, events, macros and presets for every extension point, so you never need to fork the package.
  • Fully backward compatible with the pre-2.0 BResponseSuccess/BResponseError/... API.

docs.text:

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Facades\ApiResponse;

return api()
    ->success()
    ->message('User created.')
    ->data($user)
    ->send();

// identical, via the facade
return ApiResponse::success()->message('User created.')->data($user)->send();

Default JSON shape:

{
    "status": true,
    "message": "User created.",
    "data": {
        "id": 1
    }
}

More packages

Looking for something else? Browse all bhry98 packages.

docs.title: Presets & configurable JSON structure
docs.text:
Every top-level key is renameable:

'keys' => [
    'status' => 'success',
    'message' => 'msg',
    'data' => 'result',
],

{ "success": true, "msg": "...", "result": {} }

Set 'wrap' => true to nest the whole envelope under a top-level data key.

Four built-in presets control the overall response shape (not just key names):

Preset Behaviour default The standard {status, message, data, errors?, meta?, links?} envelope. minimal Only {status, message, data, errors?} - no meta/links/extras/debug. mobile Same as default but recursively strips null values to save bandwidth. jsonapi A JSON:API-inspired {data, meta, links, errors} shape (not a strict spec implementation). 
config(['bhry98-api-response.preset' => 'minimal']); // global default

return api()->preset('jsonapi')->success()->data($user); // per response

Register your own preset:

use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Contracts\{PresetContract, ResponseFormatterContract};
use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Presets\PresetManager;

class ShoutyFormatter implements ResponseFormatterContract
{
    public function format(\Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Data\ResponsePayload $payload): array
    {
        return ['STATUS' => $payload->success, 'MESSAGE' => strtoupper($payload->message)];
    }
}

class ShoutyPreset implements PresetContract
{
    public function __construct(private ShoutyFormatter $formatter) {}
    public function formatter(): ResponseFormatterContract { return $this->formatter; }
}

// in a service provider
app(PresetManager::class)->register('shouty', ShoutyPreset::class);

return api()->preset('shouty')->success()->message('done');

docs.title: Global metadata
docs.text:
Opt in per key:

'meta' => [
    'enabled' => ['request_id', 'execution_time', 'api_version', 'locale'],
],

{ "meta": { "request_id": "...", "execution_time": "12.4ms", "api_version": "v1", "locale": "en" } }

Explicit ->meta([...]) values always win over the automatic ones on key collisions. Add your own provider by implementing MetaProviderContract and registering it under meta.providers.

There is also an optional AttachRequestId middleware that reuses an incoming X-Request-Id header (or generates one) and echoes it back as a response header, so the request_id meta stays consistent with your logs:

// bootstrap/app.php
->withMiddleware(function (Middleware $middleware) {
    $middleware->append(\Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Middleware\AttachRequestId::class);
})

docs.title: Debug mode
docs.text:
Development only - requires both flags to be true, so it can never leak into production by accident:

'debug' => [
    'enabled' => env('API_RESPONSE_DEBUG', false),
    'include' => ['queries', 'time', 'memory', 'exception', 'trace'],
],

{ "debug": { "execution_time_ms": 12.4, "memory_usage_mb": 8.1, "queries": [...] } }

docs.title: API versioning
docs.text:
'version' => env('API_RESPONSE_VERSION', 'v1'),

return api()->version('v2')->success(); // overrides for this response

Exposed automatically via the api_version meta provider when enabled.

docs.title: Translating messages
docs.text:
return api()->updated()->localize('bhry98-api-response::api.updated');

The package ships lang/en/api.php (publishable to lang/vendor/bhry98-api-response) with an entry per ready-made shortcut. config('bhry98-api-response.messages') remains the primary/default source so a config override is never silently shadowed by a translation - use localize() explicitly when you want locale-driven messages instead.

docs.title: Resolving the request's locale (Accept-Language + user column)
docs.text:
Opt-in per-request locale resolution via the api.locale middleware alias. It resolves a locale in this priority order and calls App::setLocale():

  1. The Accept-Language request header (first tag, e.g. fr out of fr-CA;q=0.9,en;q=0.5), matched against locale.supported when that list is non-empty.
  2. The authenticated user's locale column - the column name is configurable, so this works whatever your users table calls it (locale, lang, preferred_language, ...).
  3. locale.fallback (defaults to config('app.locale')).
'locale' => [
    'enabled' => env('API_RESPONSE_LOCALE_ENABLED', false),
    'supported' => ['en', 'ar', 'fr'], // empty array = accept any tag from the header
    'user_column' => env('API_RESPONSE_LOCALE_USER_COLUMN', 'locale'),
    'fallback' => env('API_RESPONSE_LOCALE_FALLBACK', config('app.locale', 'en')),
],

// bootstrap/app.php
->withMiddleware(function (Middleware $middleware) {
    $middleware->appendToGroup('api', 'api.locale');
})

Combine with the locale global metadata provider (above) to echo the resolved locale back on every response.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text:
Opt-in throttling for any route/group via the api.rate_limit middleware alias. It wraps Laravel's own RateLimiter, but returns a standard api()->tooManyRequests() envelope - with Retry-After/X-RateLimit-* headers - instead of the framework's default ThrottleRequestsException response.

'rate_limit' => [
    'enabled' => env('API_RESPONSE_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED', false),
    'max_attempts' => env('API_RESPONSE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS', 60),
    'decay_seconds' => env('API_RESPONSE_RATE_LIMIT_DECAY_SECONDS', 60),
    'by' => env('API_RESPONSE_RATE_LIMIT_BY', 'ip'), // "ip", "user" or "route"
    'key_prefix' => env('API_RESPONSE_RATE_LIMIT_PREFIX', 'api-response-rate-limit'),
    'message' => null, // null falls back to messages.too_many_requests
],

// bootstrap/app.php
->withMiddleware(function (Middleware $middleware) {
    $middleware->appendToGroup('api', 'api.rate_limit');
})

Override the configured max_attempts/decay_seconds for a specific route via middleware parameters. The second parameter is in seconds, not minutes:

Route::post('/login', ...)->middleware('api.rate_limit:5,60'); // 5 attempts per 60 seconds

by: 'user' buckets authenticated requests by the user's auth identifier and falls back to IP for guests; by: 'route' buckets by route name (or URI path when unnamed).

docs.title: Audit logging
docs.text:
Opt-in request/response auditing via the api.audit middleware alias. Every matching request is written to the api_response_audit_logs table (name configurable) through the queued StoreAuditLogEntry job by default, so logging never adds latency to the actual response - set queue.enabled to false to write synchronously instead (handy for local dev/testing).

'audit_log' => [
    'enabled' => env('API_RESPONSE_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED', false),

    'connection' => env('API_RESPONSE_AUDIT_LOG_DB_CONNECTION'), // null = default DB connection
    'table' => env('API_RESPONSE_AUDIT_LOG_TABLE', 'api_response_audit_logs'),

    'queue' => [
        'enabled' => env('API_RESPONSE_AUDIT_LOG_QUEUE_ENABLED', true),
        'connection' => env('API_RESPONSE_AUDIT_LOG_QUEUE_CONNECTION'), // null = config('queue.default')
        'queue' => env('API_RESPONSE_AUDIT_LOG_QUEUE_NAME'), // null = the connection's default queue
    ],

    'capture' => [
        'request_body' => true,
        'response_body' => true,
        'headers' => false,
    ],

    'methods' => [], // e.g. ['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'] - empty means every method
    'exclude_routes' => [], // route names or URI patterns (fnmatch), e.g. 'telescope*'

    'hidden' => [
        'password', 'password_confirmation', 'token', 'secret',
        'authorization', 'api_key', 'access_token', 'refresh_token', 'card_number', 'cvv',
    ],
],

php artisan vendor:publish --tag=bhry98-api-response-migrations
php artisan migrate

// bootstrap/app.php
->withMiddleware(function (Middleware $middleware) {
    $middleware->appendToGroup('api', 'api.audit');
})
  • queue.connection/queue.queue map directly onto StoreAuditLogEntry::onConnection()/onQueue(). Leave them null to use your app's default queue connection (config('queue.default'), e.g. sync, database, redis, ...) - set queue.connection to 'database' (or 'redis', etc.) explicitly if you want audit logs on a different connection than the rest of your app's jobs.
  • Anything listed under hidden is redacted (replaced with "***") before the entry is saved. Matching is case-insensitive and applies to keys at any depth in the request/response body, and to request headers when capture.headers is on (so Authorization is redacted by default).
  • Uploaded files are never stored. They show up in request_body as {"file": "avatar.png", "size": 1024, "mime": "image/png"}.
  • methods is case-insensitive (['post'] and ['POST'] behave the same).
  • user_id is a string column, so integer, UUID and ULID user keys all work.
  • Query the log like any other Eloquent model:
use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Models\AuditLog;

AuditLog::where('user_id', $user->id)->latest('created_at')->get();

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Run arbitrary logic against every response before it is formatted:

use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Facades\ApiResponse;
use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Data\ResponsePayload;

ApiResponse::before(function (ResponsePayload $payload) {
    $payload->extra['server'] = gethostname();
});

ApiResponse::after(function (ResponsePayload $payload) {
    Log::info('api.response', ['status' => $payload->success]);
});

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Events\ResponseCreated::class; // fired for every response
Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Events\ResponseFailed::class;  // fired when success === false
Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Events\ResponseSent::class;    // fired once the JsonResponse is built

docs.title: Exception handling
docs.text:
This is fully opt-in and off by default:

'exceptions' => [
    'override_exception_handler' => env('API_RESPONSE_OVERRIDE_EXCEPTIONS', false),

    'map' => [
        ValidationException::class => 422,
        AuthenticationException::class => 401,
        AuthorizationException::class => 403,
        ModelNotFoundException::class => 404,
        HttpExceptionInterface::class => null, // uses the exception's own status code
    ],
],

When it's enabled, exceptions thrown during JSON requests (or any api/* route) are rendered as api() responses:

Exception Response ValidationException api()->unprocessable($e->errors()), 422 AuthenticationException api()->unauthorized(), 401 AuthorizationException api()->forbidden($e->getMessage()), 403 (or the status from Gate::denyWithStatus() / denyAsNotFound()) ModelNotFoundException api()->notFound(), 404, with the generic "Resource not found." message, so model class names and IDs never reach the client any HttpExceptionInterface its own status code, message and headers (e.g. Retry-After, Allow) a class you added to map a failed response with the mapped status code and the exception's message anything else api()->internal(), 500, with the real message only when app.debug is true

Use map to change the status code of a built-in type or to register your own domain exceptions:

'map' => [
    // ...the defaults above
    App\Exceptions\InsufficientBalance::class => 409,
],

{ "status": false, "message": "Your balance is too low.", "data": null }

An explicit status on the exception itself (ValidationException::withMessages(...)->status(400), Gate::denyWithStatus(404)) always beats the map.

docs.title: Overriding the default response()->json()
docs.text:
Also fully opt-in:

'override_default_response' => env('API_RESPONSE_OVERRIDE_DEFAULT', false),

// with the flag enabled
return response()->json(['id' => 1]);
// => {"status": true, "data": {"id": 1}}

It's never forced: leave it false (the default) and response()->json() behaves exactly like stock Laravel. Responses built with api() (and the legacy BResponse* classes) are already full envelopes, so they are never wrapped a second time, whether or not this flag is on.

docs.title: Testing helpers
docs.text:
These assertions are registered automatically on Illuminate\Testing\TestResponse, so you don't need a trait or import. They respect your renamed keys and the wrap option:

$response->assertApiSuccess('User created.');
$response->assertApiError('Something went wrong.');
$response->assertApiValidation(['email']);
$response->assertApiMessage('User created.');
$response->assertApiStatus(true);
$response->assertApiData(['id' => 1]);

docs.title: Extending the package
docs.text:
• Formatters - implement ResponseFormatterContract for a fully custom envelope shape.
  • Presets - implement PresetContract and register via PresetManager::register().
  • Data resolvers - the default DataResolverContract binding (DataResolver) can be swapped in your own service provider if you need custom auto-detection.
  • Meta providers - implement MetaProviderContract, register under meta.providers, then list the key under meta.enabled.
  • Macros - ResponseBuilder::macro() / ApiResponse::macro() for one-off custom shortcuts.
  • Hooks - ApiResponse::before() / ApiResponse::after() for cross-cutting concerns (logging, request ids, ...).
  • Events - listen to ResponseCreated / ResponseFailed / ResponseSent.

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
The api() helper (and the ApiResponse facade) resolve a fresh fluent builder every time you call them - safe to chain, never shared state between responses.

use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Facades\ApiResponse;

return api()
    ->success()
    ->message('User created.')
    ->data($user)
    ->send();

// identical, via the facade
return ApiResponse::success()->message('User created.')->data($user)->send();

ResponseBuilder implements Laravel's Responsable contract, so you can skip ->send() entirely and return the builder directly from a controller or route closure:

return api()->created($user);

Default JSON shape:

{
  "status": true,
  "message": "User created.",
  "data": { "id": 1 }
}

docs.title: HTTP shortcuts
docs.text:
api()->ok($data);              // 200
api()->created($user);         // 201
api()->accepted();             // 202
api()->noContent();            // 204, empty body
api()->badRequest($msg, $errors); // 400
api()->unauthorized();         // 401
api()->forbidden();            // 403
api()->notFound();             // 404
api()->conflict();             // 409
api()->unprocessable($errors); // 422
api()->tooManyRequests();      // 429
api()->internal();             // 500
api()->serviceUnavailable();   // 503

docs.title: Business shortcuts
docs.text:
api()->saved($model);
api()->updated($model);
api()->deleted();
api()->restored($model);
api()->archived($model);
api()->verified($user);
api()->registered($user);      // 201
api()->loggedIn($user);
api()->loggedOut();
api()->passwordChanged();
api()->uploaded($file);        // 201
api()->download($url);
api()->emailSent();
api()->otpSent();

Every shortcut accepts an optional message override (api()->updated('Custom message.')) and pulls its default from config('bhry98-api-response.messages') otherwise.

docs.title: Advanced usage
docs.text:
return api()
    ->success()
    ->message('Order placed.')
    ->data($order)
    ->meta(['queue_position' => 4])
    ->links(['tracking' => route('orders.track', $order)])
    ->extra(['request_id' => (string) Str::uuid()])
    ->headers(['X-Order-Id' => $order->id])
    ->cookie(Cookie::create('last_order')->withValue($order->id))
    ->version('v2')
    ->send();
  • data() / from() - attach a payload (auto-detected, see below).
  • meta() / links() - merge into the meta / links blocks.
  • errors() - merge into the errors block (used automatically by badRequest()/unprocessable()).
  • extra() - merge extra keys into the top level of the envelope.
  • headers() / cookie() / cookies() - attach to the final JsonResponse.
  • statusCode() - set any arbitrary HTTP status.
  • preset() - pick a response shape for this call only (see Presets).
  • version() - override config('bhry98-api-response.version') for this response.
  • localize($key) - translate the current (or given) message through Laravel's translator.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Define reusable, named responses in config:

// config/bhry98-api-response.php
'responses' => [
    'user_created' => [
        'status' => true,
        'message' => 'User created successfully.',
        'code' => 201,
    ],
    'invoice_paid' => [
        'status' => true,
        'message' => 'Invoice paid.',
        'code' => 200,
    ],
],

return api()->template('user_created');

// override individual fields per call
return api()->template('user_created', ['data' => $user]);

docs.title: Macros
docs.text:
Register your own reusable responses - ResponseBuilder (and therefore api()/ApiResponse) is fully Macroable:

use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Facades\ApiResponse;

ApiResponse::macro('invoicePaid', function (Invoice $invoice) {
    /** @var \Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Builder\ResponseBuilder $this */
    return $this->success()->message('Invoice paid.')->data($invoice);
});

return api()->invoicePaid($invoice);

docs.title: Automatic data detection
docs.text:
data() (and its aliases from(), resource(), resourceCollection(), paginate()) automatically normalize whatever you pass in:

return api()->from($user);              // Eloquent model
return api()->from($users);              // Collection
return api()->from(UserResource::make($user));         // JsonResource
return api()->from(UserResource::collection($users));  // ResourceCollection
return api()->from($paginator);          // LengthAwarePaginator / CursorPaginator
return api()->from($invoiceDto);         // any Arrayable DTO
return api()->from(['id' => 1]);         // plain array - passed through untouched

Pagination and resource-collection meta/links are lifted into the envelope's top-level meta/links automatically.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
return api()->paginate($users);

{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Operation successful.",
  "data": [ ... ],
  "meta": { "current_page": 1, "last_page": 5, "per_page": 15, "total": 72, "from": 1, "to": 15 },
  "links": { "first": "...", "last": "...", "prev": null, "next": "..." }
}

Works identically for CursorPaginator and for a ResourceCollection built on top of either paginator.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
api()->resource(UserResource::make($user));
api()->resourceCollection(UserResource::collection($users));

docs.title: Upgrading to 2.1
docs.text:
composer require bhry98/laravel-api-response:^2.1

There are no breaking API changes. This release adds support for newer Laravel and PHP versions and fixes several bugs.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
• Laravel 14 is allowed (^11.0|^12.0|^13.0|^14.0) and tested against its development branch.
  • PHP 8.5 is tested on every supported Laravel version.
  • The package now requires laravel/framework directly instead of a partial list of illuminate/* components. It always relied on parts of the framework that aren't published separately (such as Illuminate\Foundation), so this only makes the real requirement explicit. Laravel apps aren't affected.

docs.title: Bug fixes
docs.text:
• No more double-wrapped responses. With override_default_response enabled, api() responses (and the legacy BResponse* ones) used to be wrapped a second time: {"status": true, "data": {"status": true, "message": ...}}. They are now always sent exactly once.
  • exceptions.map is now applied. The map in the config used to be ignored. You can now remap built-in exceptions and register your own exception classes with a status code. See Exception handling.
  • ModelNotFoundException no longer leaks internals. Laravel converts it to a NotFoundHttpException before render callbacks run, so the response used to say No query results for model [App\Models\User] 5. It now returns the generic "Resource not found." message.
  • AuthorizationException keeps its status. Gate::denyWithStatus() / denyAsNotFound() statuses are respected.
  • HTTP exception headers are kept. Retry-After, Allow and other headers on an HttpException now reach the client.
  • Audit log: Authorization headers are redacted. With capture.headers on, header values (which are arrays) were never redacted, so bearer tokens ended up in the log. Hidden keys are now redacted at every level.
  • Audit log: file uploads work with the queue. Requests that contained an uploaded file made the queued job fail, because uploaded files can't be serialized. They are now stored as a {file, size, mime} description.
  • Audit log: smaller fixes. methods is case-insensitive, and user agents longer than 255 characters are truncated instead of breaking the insert on MySQL.
  • Debug info from ->trace() is kept when the global debug block is enabled. The global block used to overwrite it.
  • localize() ignores a key that resolves to a whole translation group (an array) instead of throwing a TypeError.
  • Locale resolution ignores Accept-Language tags with q=0, which means "not acceptable".
  • Testing macros (assertApiSuccess(), assertApiValidation(), ...) now work when wrap is enabled.
  • Exception rendering is now registered even if the exception handler was resolved before the package's service provider booted.
  • The rate-limit docs example was wrong: api.rate_limit:5,1 means 5 attempts per second. Use api.rate_limit:5,60 for 5 per minute.

docs.title: Optional: audit log user_id column
docs.text:
New installs create user_id as a string(64) column, so UUID and ULID user keys fit. If you already ran the old migration and your users have non-integer keys, change the column yourself:

Schema::table('api_response_audit_logs', function (Blueprint $table) {
    $table->string('user_id', 64)->nullable()->change();
});

Integer user keys keep working with the old column, so you don't need to do anything for them.

docs.title: Backward compatibility & migration
docs.text:
The pre-2.0 API (BResponseSuccess, BResponseError, BResponseValidationError, BResponseNotFound, BResponseInternalError and the underlying Helpers\BaseResponse) still works unchanged and is not going away - it is marked @deprecated in favor of api()/ApiResponse, nothing more.

One behavioral fix ships alongside: previously toJson() duplicated (and diverged from) toArray()'s logic, ignoring config('keys')/config('wrap') entirely and emitting the raw HTTP status code as the status value. toJson() now simply delegates to toArray(), so both honor your configured keys/wrap, and status is a boolean (< 400) as documented - matching the shape every new response produced by api() already used.

// still works exactly as before
use Bhry98\LaravelApiResponse\Facades\BResponseSuccess;

return BResponseSuccess::make()
    ->message('Everything is fine!')
    ->data(['id' => 1])
    ->additions(['request_id' => uniqid()])
    ->toJson();

docs.title: New in 2.0
docs.text:
Three cross-cutting concerns joined the package as opt-in middleware, each config-driven with sensible defaults - nothing below changes behavior until you turn it on:

  • Rate limiting (api.rate_limit) - see Customization → Rate limiting.
  • Audit logging (api.audit) - see Customization → Audit logging. Requires publishing and running the new migration if you enable it.
  • Locale resolution (api.locale) - see Customization → Localization.

If you're upgrading from a version before these existed, re-publish the config to pick up the new rate_limit, audit_log and locale sections:

php artisan vendor:publish --tag=bhry98-api-response-config --force

(Back up any custom edits to config/bhry98-api-response.php first - --force overwrites the whole file.)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
src/
  Builder/        ResponseBuilder + its Concerns traits (fluent state, HTTP/business shortcuts, templates, terminal methods)
  Contracts/      Interfaces: ResponseBuilderContract, ResponseFormatterContract, PresetContract, DataResolverContract, MetaProviderContract, PipelineStageContract
  Data/           ResponsePayload (the mutable value object threaded through the pipeline)
  Enums/          MetaKey, Preset
  Events/         ResponseCreated, ResponseFailed, ResponseSent
  Exceptions/     TemplateNotFoundException, PresetNotFoundException, ExceptionRenderer
  Facades/        ApiResponse (+ deprecated legacy facades)
  Formatters/     DefaultFormatter, MinimalFormatter, MobileFormatter, JsonApiFormatter
  Helpers/        Legacy BaseResponse / ResponseKeys (deprecated, BC only)
  Hooks/          HookRegistry (before/after)
  Jobs/           StoreAuditLogEntry (queued audit log writer)
  Middleware/     AttachRequestId, ApiRateLimit, AuditRequests, ResolveLocale (all optional)
  Models/         AuditLog
  Pipeline/       ResponsePipeline + Stages (data resolution, global meta, debug, hooks, events)
  Presets/        PresetManager + built-in presets
  Providers/      BResponseServiceProvider
  Responses/      Legacy per-type response classes (deprecated, BC only)
  Support/        DataResolver, MetaProviderRegistry, DebugCollector, meta providers, response-factory override
  Testing/        TestResponse assertion macros
database/
  migrations/     Publishable audit_log table migration

Every piece is bound through the container and swappable - nothing is a static god-class, and ResponseBuilder itself is always resolved fresh (never a singleton) so fluent state is never shared between responses.
